account.activity_title.context: Settings > Account: heading of the card that lists account notices and recent sign-ins.

account.latest.context: Settings > Security, card 'Account activity': the latest event of the account. {event} = what happened (e.g. 'Signed in', 'Failed sign-in'), {when} = its date and time.

account.notices_count.context: Settings > Security, card 'Account activity': badge with the number of notices that need the person's attention.

account.notices_empty.context: Settings > Account > Account activity: shown under the Notices sub-heading when there is nothing to report.

account.notices_title.context: Settings > Account > Account activity: sub-heading of the list of security notices about this account (recovery key used, two-factor sign-in reset...).

account.review.context: Button on the Security card 'Account activity': opens the notices and the recent sign-ins.

account.signins_empty.context: Settings > Account > Account activity: shown under Recent sign-ins when the history is empty.

account.signins_load_failed.context: Settings > Account > Account activity: red alert next to the Try again button when the sign-in history could not be loaded.

account.signins_show_all.context: Button under Recent sign-ins (Settings > Account > Account activity) when the history has more than three rows: shows the whole list. {count} = how many sign-ins it will show (a number, never 1, 2 or 3). Short: it sits under the list on a phone.

account.signins_show_fewer.context: Button under Recent sign-ins (Settings > Account > Account activity) once the whole list is shown: goes back to the three latest. Same place as account.signins_show_all, which it replaces.

account.signins_title.context: Settings > Account > Account activity: sub-heading of the history of recent sign-ins (newest first).

action.deselect.context: Button in the row menu of a message that is ticked (selected): takes it out of the selection.

action.move_to_folder.context: Button that opens a list of folders (in the row menu of a message and in the bar of a selection): moves the message or messages to the folder chosen.

action.select.context: Button in the row menu of a message: ticks it and starts a selection, so several messages can be archived, moved or labelled at once.

activity.agent_on.context: Sign-in history row, second line: the browser and the operating system of the device, e.g. "Firefox on Windows". {browser} = browser name (Firefox, Chrome...), {system} = operating system name (Windows, macOS...); both are product names and stay as they are.

activity.device_ip.context: Sign-in history row, second line: the device text and the IP address it signed in from. {device} = text such as "Firefox on Windows", {ip} = the IP address (kept as is).

activity.kind.2fa_reset.context: Sign-in history row title: the two-factor sign-in of the account was reset (by an admin).

activity.kind.2fa_reset_pending.context: Sign-in history row title: an admin scheduled a reset of the two-factor sign-in that has not taken effect yet.

activity.kind.break_glass.context: Sign-in history row title: the administrator account was restored with the deployment's setup key.

activity.kind.first_sign_in.context: Sign-in history row title: the first sign-in with the temporary password given by an admin, after which the person chooses a password.

activity.kind.locked_delete_requested.context: Title of a row in the sign-in history: the deletion of the old mail that is locked under the replaced key was requested. vi and zh-CN are cyber's (overrides); no need to translate.

activity.kind.password_recovered.context: Sign-in history row title: the password was reset by the person with their recovery key (not by an admin).

activity.kind.recovery_key_replaced.context: Sign-in history row title: the recovery key was replaced by a new one.

activity.kind.recovery_started.context: Sign-in history row title: someone started a password reset with the recovery key.

activity.kind.sign_in.context: Sign-in history row title: an ordinary successful sign-in.

activity.kind_unknown.context: Sign-in history row title (and event name in a notice) for a kind of event this version does not know. {kind} = the raw code from the server (kept as is, e.g. brand_new).

activity.notice_2fa_reset.context: Account notice (Settings > Account > Notices): the two-factor sign-in was reset and no admin is named. {date} = date and time of the reset.

activity.notice_2fa_reset_by.context: Account notice (Settings > Account > Notices): an admin reset the two-factor sign-in. {admin} = the admin's address, {date} = date and time of the reset.

activity.notice_2fa_reset_pending.context: Notice for an ADMIN: another admin asked to reset their two-factor sign-in; it takes effect at {due} (a date and time, 24 hours later) unless cancelled. {admin} is an email address.

activity.notice_alert_2fa_reset.context: Alert for an admin: another admin reset someone's two-factor sign-in. {admin} and {target} are email addresses.

activity.notice_alert_2fa_reset_cancelle.context: Alert for an admin: an admin cancelled the pending reset of their own two-factor sign-in. {target} is an email address.

activity.notice_alert_2fa_reset_pending.context: Alert for an admin: another admin asked to reset the two-factor sign-in of an admin; it takes effect at {due} unless that person cancels.

activity.notice_alert_account_delete.context: Alert for an admin: another admin deleted an account.

activity.notice_alert_admin_created.context: Alert for an admin: another admin created a new admin account.

activity.notice_alert_break_glass.context: Alert for an admin: an admin account was restored with the deployment's setup key (break-glass).

activity.notice_alert_break_glass_failur.context: Notice for every ADMIN: {count} (a number, ten today) failed attempts to use the deployment setup key within one hour; the alert is raised at the TENTH failure, and {date} is the time of that tenth one (later failures are not added). Says what to check. Same facts as the push text push.alert_break_glass_failures.body. "Setup key" is the glossary term.

activity.notice_alert_require_2fa_relaxe.context: Alert for an admin: another admin turned off the organisation-wide requirement of two-factor sign-in.

activity.notice_alert_role_change.context: Alert for an admin: another admin changed the role of an account. {role} is Admin or Member (already translated).

activity.notice_alert_temp_password_reis.context: Alert for an admin: another admin issued a new temporary password for an account that has not signed in yet.

activity.notice_break_glass.context: Notice for an ADMIN whose password and keys were replaced with the setup key (break-glass). It must say that the password and keys were reset and that the earlier mail stays locked, like the push text of the same event. cyber CAT-6.

activity.notice_generic.context: Account notice for a kind of event without its own sentence. {event} = the event title (a text such as "Recovery key replaced"), {date} = date and time.

activity.notice_generic_by.context: Same as the generic account notice, when an admin did it. {event} = the event title, {admin} = the admin's address, {date} = date and time.

activity.notice_locked_delete_requested.context: Notice (banner and account activity card) for the OWNER: somebody who knew the password and passed the second step asked to delete the old mail that is locked under the owner's previous (replaced) key. {date} is when it was asked, {due} when it will be deleted (a date and time); a Cancel button sits under the text. Same facts as the push text push.locked_delete_requested.body. vi and zh-CN are cyber's (overrides); no need to translate.

activity.notice_password_recovered.context: Account notice (Settings > Account > Notices): the password was reset with the recovery key. {date} = date and time. Asks the person to act if it was not them.

activity.notice_recovery_key_replaced.context: Account notice (Settings > Account > Notices): the recovery key was replaced. {date} = date and time.

activity.notice_recovery_started.context: Account notice (Settings > Account > Notices): someone used the recovery key to start a password reset. {date} = date and time. Asks the person to create a new recovery key if it was not them.

activity.notice_second_factor_locked.context: Notice (banner and account activity card) for the OWNER of an account: after the password was right, wrong authenticator or recovery codes were entered too often, so sign-in with a code is paused: 15 minutes for the first two pauses, 24 hours from the third (the Worker's SECOND_FACTOR_POLICY). {date} is a date and time. Tells the person what to do if it was not them. Same facts as the push text push.second_factor_locked.body.

activity.sign_in_failed.context: Sign-in history row title for a failed sign-in attempt (wrong password or code).

activity.unknown_device.context: Sign-in history row, second line: shown when the browser and system could not be told from the device information.

admin.checking.context: Button label while a check runs: the step-up code is being verified, or a domain DNS check is running.

admin.close_console.context: aria-label of the icon-only close (X) button in the admin console header. Screen reader only.

admin.col_actions.context: Admin console tables (Domains, and the extra addresses in a person's dialog): header of the column of row buttons. Screen reader only (the header is not shown).

admin.domains_desc.context: Admin console, Domains page: the one line under the page title.

admin.people_desc.context: Admin console, People page: the one line under the page title.

admin.policy_confirm_label.context: Admin Settings, two-factor rule: label of the field where the admin types their own address before the rule is relaxed. {address} is that address.

admin.policy_confirm_mismatch.context: Admin Settings, two-factor rule: error under the confirmation field when the typed text is not the admin's address. {address} is that address.

admin.policy_desc.context: Admin Settings, two-factor rule: the one line under the card title.

admin.policy_off_body.context: Admin Settings, two-factor rule: the question shown before the requirement is turned off for members.

admin.policy_off_effect.context: Admin Settings, two-factor rule: hint under the switch while the requirement is off (who it affects).

admin.policy_on_effect.context: Admin Settings, two-factor rule: hint under the switch while the requirement is on (who it affects).

admin.policy_switch.context: Admin Settings, two-factor rule: label of the switch.

admin.policy_title.context: Admin Settings: title of the card with the two-factor rule of the organisation.

admin.policy_turn_off.context: Admin Settings, two-factor rule: the button that confirms turning the requirement off (destructive).

admin.sections_label.context: aria-label of the tab list of the admin console (People, Domains, Audit log). Screen reader only.

admin.settings_desc.context: Admin console, Settings page: the one line under the page title.

admin.step_up_body.context: Step-up dialog: explains why the code is asked.

admin.step_up_code.context: Step-up dialog: label of the 6-digit code field.

admin.step_up_title.context: Title of the dialog that asks for an authenticator code before an admin change goes through.

admin.tab_domains.context: Admin console tab: the domains the deployment offers addresses on (plural; the glossary term Domain is singular).

admin.tab_people.context: Admin console tab: the list of accounts.

app.account_named.context: Accessible name of the round avatar button in the header (the only way into Settings). {initials} = the letters shown in the circle (e.g. 'AM' or '李'), so a voice-control user can say what they see. Same words as app.account_settings after them.

app.account_settings.context: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the round avatar button in the header (opens Settings)

app.action_failed.context: Toast when a mail action (archive, star, mark all read...) fails and the server gave no reason

app.clear_search.context: Screen-reader label of the X button inside the search box

app.draft_unavailable.context: Toast when a draft clicked in the Drafts folder cannot be opened

app.file_badge.context: Badge on an attachment whose file name has no extension (otherwise the badge shows e.g. PDF); a 4-letter square

app.forward_header_date.context: Line of the forwarded-message header inside the OUTGOING mail body: the date of the original

app.forward_header_from.context: Line of the forwarded-message header inside the OUTGOING mail body: the original sender, {sender} is 'Name <address>'

app.forward_header_subject.context: Line of the forwarded-message header inside the OUTGOING mail body: the original subject

app.forward_header_title.context: First line of the forwarded-message header inside the OUTGOING mail body (a divider line); keep the dashes

app.labels_failed.context: Toast when adding or removing a label on a message fails

app.load_more_failed.context: Toast when the 'Load more' button of the message list fails

app.mark_all_read.context: Phone header icon button (tooltip and screen-reader label): marks every unread message of the list as read

app.message_unavailable.context: Toast when the selected message cannot be loaded (deleted meanwhile, old notification link)

app.new_messages.context: Read out by screen readers (not shown) when new mail arrives in the open folder

app.no_connection.context: Toast when a request fails because the device is offline (also the prefix of every failed action)

app.no_content.context: Shown in the reader in place of the body when a message has no text at all

app.open_mailboxes.context: Screen-reader label of the hamburger button on phones that opens the folder drawer

app.position.context: Reader toolbar: place of the open message in the list, e.g. '3 of 25'

app.refresh_failed.context: Toast when the Refresh button of the message list fails

app.reply_quote_header.context: First line of the quoted original inside the OUTGOING reply body: 'On <date>, <name> wrote:' ({date} is a numeric date and time; {name} is the sender's name and address, 'Priya Nair <priya@example.com>')

app.retry_in.context: Status line on the 'Could not reach the server' screen, under the explanation: the app checks again on its own; {seconds} counts down (5, 4, 3...). Short.

app.retrying.context: Status line on the 'Could not reach the server' screen while the app is checking the connection again. Short.

app.search_mail.context: Placeholder of the search box and its hidden label

app.search_results.context: Shown under the heading of a search (and read out by screen readers when it finishes): how many messages it found and where. {more} is '+' when more pages exist, else empty; {scope} = the folder's name (Inbox, Archive...) or 'All mail'.

app.server_unreachable.context: Full-screen text when the first session check cannot reach the server (above a 'Try again' button); also the Settings > Notifications error when the server cannot be reached

app.server_unreachable_hint.context: Line under 'Could not reach the server.' on the full-screen status page (above the 'Try again' button): what to check, and that the app keeps trying by itself

app.skip_to_message.context: Second skip link at the very top of the desktop mailbox (shown only when it has keyboard focus): jumps past the list to the message open on the right, where Reply and the other actions are.

app.skip_to_messages.context: Skip link: the first thing the Tab key reaches in the mailbox, shown only while it has keyboard focus; moves focus straight to the message list

app.snooze_failed.context: Toast fallback when snoozing a message fails and the server gave no reason

app.subtitle_drafts#one.context: Small text next to the Drafts title when nothing is unread: count of drafts ({more} is '+' when more pages exist, else empty)

app.subtitle_messages#one.context: Small text next to the folder title when nothing is unread: count of messages ({more} is '+' when more pages exist, else empty)

app.subtitle_unread.context: Small text next to the folder title: count of unread messages ({more} is '+' when more pages exist, else empty)

app.theme_to_dark.context: Name and tooltip of the header theme button while the light theme is on (the button switches to dark)

app.theme_to_light.context: Name and tooltip of the header theme button while the dark theme is on (the button switches to light)

app.title_unread.context: Browser tab title part: the open folder and its number of unread messages, e.g. 'Inbox (2)'; the app adds ' - Edging Mail'

audit.action.2fa_disabled.context: Audit log row: the person turned two-factor sign-in off.

audit.action.2fa_enabled.context: Audit log row: the person turned two-factor sign-in on.

audit.action.2fa_reset.context: Audit log row: an admin reset the two-factor sign-in of an account.

audit.action.2fa_reset_cancelled.context: Audit log row: the admin cancelled the waiting reset of their two-factor sign-in by signing in.

audit.action.2fa_reset_requested.context: Audit log row: a reset of an admin's two-factor sign-in was requested and waits before it takes effect.

audit.action.alias.add.context: Audit log row: an admin added an extra address (alias) to an account.

audit.action.alias.remove.context: Audit log row: an admin removed an extra address (alias) from an account.

audit.action.break_glass.context: Audit log row: an admin account was restored with the deployment setup key.

audit.action.domain.add.context: Audit log row: an admin added a domain.

audit.action.domain.remove.context: Audit log row: an admin removed a domain.

audit.action.keys_created.context: Audit log row: the encryption keys of an account were created.

audit.action.locked_mail_delete_canceled.context: Row in the admin audit log: the person cancelled that request before its date.

audit.action.locked_mail_delete_requeste.context: Row in the admin audit log: a person asked to delete the old mail that is locked under their replaced key (the log shows who and which key, never the mail).

audit.action.locked_mail_deleted.context: Row in the admin audit log: the scheduled job deleted the locked mail after the waiting time (the actor is the scheduled job).

audit.action.password_change.context: Audit log row: the person changed their password.

audit.action.password_recovered.context: Audit log row: the person set a new password with their recovery key.

audit.action.recovery.context: Audit log row: an admin account was restored (older entries).

audit.action.recovery_code_used.context: Audit log row: a sign-in used one of the recovery codes.

audit.action.recovery_codes_regenerated.context: Audit log row: the person made a new set of recovery codes.

audit.action.recovery_key_replaced.context: Audit log row: the person created a new recovery key.

audit.action.recovery_started.context: Audit log row: someone started a password recovery with a recovery key.

audit.action.sessions_revoked.context: Audit log row: the person signed out their other devices (every other session of the account ended; the device they used stays signed in).

audit.action.settings.default_language.context: Audit log row: an admin changed the default language of the organisation.

audit.action.settings.require_2fa.context: Audit log row: an admin changed whether everyone must use two-factor sign-in.

audit.action.setup.context: Audit log row: the first admin set up the deployment.

audit.action.sign_in.context: Audit log row: a successful sign-in.

audit.action.sign_in_failed.context: Audit log row: a failed sign-in.

audit.action.temp_password_expired.context: Audit log row: someone tried to sign in with a temporary password that had expired.

audit.action.temp_password_reissued.context: Audit log row: an admin issued a new temporary password to a person who had not signed in yet.

audit.action.user.create.context: Audit log row: an admin created an account.

audit.action.user.delete.context: Audit log row: an admin deleted an account.

audit.action.user.disable.context: Audit log row: an admin disabled an account.

audit.action.user.enable.context: Audit log row: an admin enabled an account.

audit.action.user.first_sign_in.context: Audit log row: the first sign-in of a new account, with its temporary password.

audit.action.user.rename.context: Audit log row: an admin changed the display name of an account.

audit.action.user.role_change.context: Audit log row: an admin changed the role of an account (Admin or Member).

audit.action_unknown.context: Audit log row title for an action this app has no text for yet. {action} is the raw action code, shown as it is.

audit.actor_scheduled.context: Audit log: who did it, when the server did it on its own schedule (no person).

audit.actor_to_target.context: Audit log row: who did it and to whom. {actor} and {target} are email addresses (or a domain name).

audit.detail_aliases.context: Audit log row detail name: how many extra addresses the first admin set up (lower case, before a colon).

audit.detail_change.context: Audit log detail of a change: from the old value to the new one (Member to Admin, Off to On, one language to another).

audit.detail_deleted.context: Audit log row detail name: how many locked messages were deleted (lower case, before a colon).

audit.detail_due.context: Audit log row detail name: when a delayed two-factor reset takes effect (lower case, before a colon). The value is a date and time.

audit.detail_from.context: Audit log row detail name: the old value of a change (lower case, before a colon).

audit.detail_key.context: Audit log row detail name: the id of an encryption key (lower case, before a colon).

audit.detail_pair.context: Audit log row: one detail of the entry. {label} is the name of the detail, {value} its value. Several are shown side by side, separated by a dot.

audit.detail_reason.context: Audit log row detail name: why a sign-in failed (lower case, before a colon).

audit.detail_recovery_code.context: Audit log row detail value: the sign-in used a recovery code.

audit.detail_role.context: Audit log row detail name: the role of a new account (lower case, before a colon).

audit.detail_second_factor.context: Audit log row detail name: which second step a sign-in used (lower case, before a colon).

audit.detail_to.context: Audit log row detail name: the new value of a change (lower case, before a colon).

audit.detail_user.context: Audit log row detail name: the account an extra address belongs to (lower case, before a colon).

audit.empty.context: Admin Audit log tab when the log is empty.

audit.end.context: Admin Audit log tab: shown under the list when there are no more entries.

audit.end_range.context: Audit log: under the list when every event of the chosen date range is shown (older ones exist).

audit.filter_clear.context: Audit log: button that resets both filters when nothing matches.

audit.filter_date.context: Audit log: label of the filter by date range (Last 7 days, Last 30 days, All time).

audit.filter_kind.context: Audit log: label of the filter by kind of event.

audit.filter_none.context: Audit log: shown when the filters leave no event.

audit.filter_person.context: Audit log: label of the filter by the person who did the action.

audit.intro.context: Admin Audit log tab: line above the list.

audit.kind_accounts.context: Audit log, Event filter: account and alias changes.

audit.kind_all.context: Audit log, Event filter: no filter.

audit.kind_security.context: Audit log, Event filter: sign-ins, passwords, keys, two-factor.

audit.kind_settings.context: Audit log, Event filter: changes of the organisation settings.

audit.loading.context: Admin Audit log tab while the log loads (spinner and text).

audit.person_all.context: Audit log, Done by filter: no filter.

audit.range_30.context: Audit log, date filter: events of the last 30 days.

audit.range_7.context: Audit log, date filter: events of the last 7 days (the default).

audit.range_all.context: Audit log, date filter: every event.

audit.reason_disabled.context: Audit log detail, reason of a failed sign-in: the account is disabled.

audit.reason_not_admin.context: Audit log detail, reason a scheduled reset was cancelled: the admin who requested it was disabled, deleted or made a member.

audit.reason_second_factor.context: Audit log detail, reason of a failed sign-in: the two-factor code was wrong.

audit.reason_wrong_password.context: Audit log detail, reason of a failed sign-in: the password was wrong.

audit.show_older.context: Audit log: button under the list that widens the date filter to All time.

audit.value_off.context: Audit log detail value: a rule was off.

audit.value_on.context: Audit log detail value: a rule was on (e.g. the two-factor requirement).

auth.address_invalid.context: Shown when the typed address is not a full email address (checked in the browser), and under the address field of Restore an admin account (break-glass) when Continue was pressed with it empty. name@example.com is only an example.

auth.code_label.context: Label of the field for the six digits of the authenticator app.

auth.email_label.context: Label of the email address field on the sign-in screen.

auth.forgot_hint.context: Sign-in screen: one quiet line under the password field, about the 'Forgot password' link (auth.forgot_password) on the field's label row. Resetting the password needs the recovery key the person saved when the account was set up. Screen readers also read it as the link's description.

auth.forgot_password.context: Button: a text link on the label row of the password field (sign-in and unlock) that opens the forgotten-password flow (no question mark: it is a button).

auth.panel_proof_host.context: Brand panel of the sign-in screens (desktop, right half): the second of three short proof lines under the statement, with a building icon. The app runs on the organisation's own account, not a mail provider's.

auth.panel_proof_no_admin.context: Brand panel of the sign-in screens (desktop, right half): the first of three short proof lines under the statement, with a lock icon. Mail is encrypted to each person's own key, so nobody else can open it, admins included (as forgot.lost_key says).

auth.panel_proof_two_factor.context: Brand panel of the sign-in screens (desktop, right half): the third of three short proof lines, with a shield icon. Admin accounts always have two-factor sign-in (members when the organisation requires it).

auth.panel_statement.context: Brand panel of the sign-in screens (desktop, right half): one large statement in display type. Mail is stored encrypted and only the person's password, in their own browser, opens it.

auth.password_required.context: Sign-in, unlock, and the password asked once more after a reload in the middle of a first sign-in: red line under the password field after the person pressed the button with the field empty.

auth.recovery_code_hint.context: Hint under the recovery-code field: such a code only signs the person in; it cannot open mail.

auth.recovery_code_label.context: Label of the field for ONE two-factor recovery code (not the recovery key).

auth.recovery_code_lead.context: Second sign-in step when the person chose a two-factor recovery code instead of the app code.

auth.recovery_code_required.context: Second step of sign-in, recovery-code mode: red line under the recovery code field after Verify was pressed with it empty.

auth.second_step_lead.context: Under the heading of the second sign-in step.

auth.second_step_title.context: Heading of the second sign-in step (code from the authenticator app).

auth.shared_device.context: Checkbox label on the sign-in and unlock screens: the key stays in memory only.

auth.shared_device_hint.context: Hint under the shared-device checkbox on the sign-in screen: the encryption key stays in this browser tab only, but closing the tab does not end the sign-in. "Sign out" is the catalogue label of the sign-out button. cyber CAT-15.

auth.shared_device_short.context: Sign-in, unlock and first-sign-in screens: short line under the shared-device checkbox, always shown, saying what ticking it changes for the person (subject: the choice): the encryption key is kept in this tab's memory only, so the password is asked again once the tab is closed or reloaded (the session itself stays signed in). Once the box is ticked the longer auth.shared_device_hint replaces it.

auth.show_key.context: Button (icon only): eye icon inside a setup-key field (first-run Setup, Restore an admin account) that shows the typed key; aria-label, no visible text. It keeps this name while the key is shown (its pressed state says so).

auth.step.context: Screens before the mailbox (first-run Setup, Forgot password, Restore an admin account, the steps of a first sign-in): small line above the title, beside a thin progress bar. {current} is the number of this step and {total} the number of steps (2 or 3).

auth.trust_line.context: Sign-in and unlock screens: one quiet line with a lock icon at the foot of the card. A true claim (docs/security.md): mail is stored encrypted, and the server never receives the password (only a value derived from it). Do not make it a bigger promise (not 'end-to-end' for all mail, not 'nobody can ever read').

auth.try_again_in.context: Added after an error when the server asks the person to wait. {seconds} counts down.

auth.use_app_code.context: Button: link that switches the second step back to the authenticator app code.

auth.use_recovery_code.context: Button: link that switches the second step to a two-factor recovery code.

auth.verify.context: Button: submits the code of the second sign-in step.

breakglass.address.context: Label of the admin email address field.

breakglass.done_title.context: Heading when the admin account was restored.

breakglass.key_lead.context: Under the heading of the new recovery key screen of break-glass.

breakglass.lead.context: Under the heading: only for admins who lost both password and recovery key; needs the deployment's setup key.

breakglass.old_mail.context: Honest consequence: mail sealed to the old key stays locked after break-glass.

breakglass.setup_key.context: Label of the setup key field.

docs.arch_cron.context: CAT-21. Card text: what the every-minute job does: returns snoozed mail, seals mail that waited for its owner to set up keys, converts old unencrypted mail from the single-user version; and (new) applies two-factor resets that are due (an admin's reset of another admin waits 24 hours) and, seven days after a person asked, deletes their locked old mail (mail sealed to a key that was replaced).

docs.arch_cron_title.context: Card title: the scheduled job (cron) that runs every minute.

docs.arch_d1.context: CAT-22. Card text: what is stored in D1, and what is NOT encrypted there. "Sealed" = encrypted so that only the owner can read it. The mail index keeps sender, recipients, dates, sizes and labels readable (unencrypted); subject, text and attachment names are encrypted. Keep both halves.

docs.arch_d1_title.context: Card title: D1 is the name of Cloudflare's SQLite database product; never translated.

docs.arch_inbound.context: Card text in the Architecture tab. Cloudflare Email Routing hands the message to the Worker (the server program). "Sealed to that person's key" = encrypted so that only that person can open it; keep the glossary words for sealing and key. DATA_KEY is the name of a server secret: keep it as it is. An address with no account is rejected.

docs.arch_inbound_title.context: Card title in the Architecture tab: how incoming mail is received.

docs.arch_keys.context: Card text. {data_key} is the name of a secret (never translated). It protects what the server must read back itself, including mail that arrives before its owner has set up keys.

docs.arch_keys_title.context: Card title in the Architecture tab: how keys and secrets are used.

docs.arch_outbound.context: CAT-20. Card text. Mail to other servers goes out through Cloudflare Email Sending. Mail between two people on this same deployment is encrypted in the sender's browser and stays inside, BUT ONLY when every recipient has set up encryption keys and the message is within the size limits; otherwise the server can read it (a copy for a person without keys is sent unencrypted to the server; a message that is too large goes out through Email Sending and comes back in). Keep both conditions and both exceptions (do not call it "end-to-end encrypted" here: that term is for the badge only).

list.unread_sr.context: Screen-reader only text before an unread message row

locked.banner#one.context: Card above the mailbox, singular ({count} is 1). After an admin restored their account with the setup key, mail that arrived before is sealed to the OLD encryption key; only the recovery key they had then can open it, so this browser cannot. Calm, factual; a 'Why?' button and two buttons follow (Keep it locked, Delete it…). Glossary: message, key, encrypt.

locked.cancel.context: Button that stops a deletion of locked old mail that was asked for and is waiting for its date (on the locked-mail card and on the notice). vi and zh-CN are cyber's (overrides); no need to translate.

locked.card_title.context: Settings > Security: title of the card about old messages that are locked under a replaced key (Delete, or the planned date and Cancel).

locked.confirm_label.context: Label of the field in the confirmation dialog where the person types their own email address, which is shown in the label ({address}), so a stray click cannot start the deletion.

locked.confirm_mismatch.context: Delete locked mail dialog: red line under the address field after Delete was pressed while the address typed is not the own one.

locked.delete.context: Button on the locked-mail card that opens the confirmation, and the red button of that confirmation (title: Delete locked mail). It does not delete at once.

locked.delete_them.context: Button on the locked-mail card (danger style): opens the confirmation that deletes the locked messages (it asks for the address, the password and the code, then waits seven days). {count} = how many are locked; the word only changes for one.

locked.dialog_body#one.context: First line of the confirmation dialog, singular. Deleted locked mail cannot be brought back.

locked.dialog_note.context: Plain note under the first line of the confirmation dialog: the server waits several days before deleting, and the person can cancel in that time. Do not write the number of days.

locked.dialog_title.context: Title of the confirmation dialog that asks for the address, the password and (with two-factor sign-in) the authenticator code before locked messages are scheduled for deletion.

locked.keep_locked.context: Button on the locked-mail card: leave the locked messages where they are and put the card away for now. Nothing is sent to the server. {count} = how many are locked; the word only changes for one.

locked.not_pending.context: Second line of the notice about a requested deletion of locked mail, shown when the deletion is not waiting any more (the person cancelled it, or it has been carried out).

locked.pending#one.context: Card above the mailbox while a deletion of locked mail waits for its date, singular. {date} is a date and time; the person can cancel until then (Cancel deletion button next to it).

locked.region.context: Landmark label (read by screen readers) of the card above the mailbox that tells the person that some old messages are locked.

locked.why.context: Small button on the locked-mail card (a disclosure: it opens in place) that shows one paragraph explaining why the older messages cannot be opened. A verb, no final punctuation.

locked.why_text.context: The answer under 'See why' on the locked-mail card. Plain words for a non-expert. Glossary: setup key, encryption key, recovery key.

login.signing_in.context: Label of the sign-in button while the password is being checked

mailcrypto.download_raw.context: Button: text button at the bottom of the reader that saves the original message as an .eml file.

mailcrypto.images_hidden.context: Line above the mail frame in the reader when the message has pictures embedded in it (not remote ones) and the person has not chosen Show images yet; the Show images button sits next to it.

mailcrypto.note_failed.context: Reader body when a message arrived but could not be opened in the browser (damaged data or an unexpected format).

mailcrypto.note_locked.context: Reader body when no key is unlocked in the browser yet, so no message can be opened.

mailcrypto.note_other_key.context: Reader body for a message that was encrypted to a key other than the one now in use (for example after an admin recovery of the account). Says only what this browser can do; it does not claim who else can or cannot open it.

mailcrypto.note_pending.context: Reader body for a message that arrived before the person had a key and has not been sealed to their key yet.

mailcrypto.subject_failed.context: Shown in place of the subject (list row and reader heading) for a message that could not be opened.

mailcrypto.subject_locked.context: Shown in place of the subject (list row and reader heading) for a message that is locked: no key unlocked yet, or sealed to another key.

mailcrypto.subject_pending.context: Shown in place of the subject (list row and reader heading) for a message still being prepared for the person's key.

notice.cancel_reset.context: Button on the notice about a pending reset of the person's two-factor sign-in: stops the reset.

notice.dismiss.context: Button on a notice in the banner: hides it for good.

notice.dismiss_from.context: Quiet line under a notice that cannot be dismissed yet (security notices stay seven days); the Dismiss button appears from then on. {date} is a date and time.

notice.fewer.context: Button under the account notices above the mailbox when the other notices are shown: hides them again, leaving the most urgent one.

notice.more.context: Button (link style) under the banner when there are more than three notices: opens Settings, Account tab, where all of them are listed.

notice.more_count.context: Button under the most urgent account notice above the mailbox: shows the others. {count} = how many more.

notice.region.context: Accessible name of the banner above the mailbox that lists account notices. Read by screen readers only.

password.check_failed.context: Password field status line (red alert) when the data of the common-password check could not be loaded; a Try again link follows it.

password.check_loading.context: Password field status line with a spinner while the data of the common-password check loads.

password.level_fair.context: Password strength result shown under the password field (second level) and spoken by the strength meter.

password.level_good.context: Password strength result shown under the password field (third level) and spoken by the strength meter.

password.level_strong.context: Password strength result shown under the password field (highest level) and spoken by the strength meter.

password.level_weak.context: Password strength result shown under the password field (lowest level; also the level of a refused password) and spoken by the strength meter.

password.meter_empty.context: Screen reader value of the password strength bar while the field is empty (aria-valuetext). Not shown on screen.

password.meter_label.context: Screen reader name of the password strength bar (aria-label of the meter under the password field). Not shown on screen.

password.problem_common.context: Password field status line: the password is on the lists of common passwords (also with digits, symbols or look-alike letters added).

password.problem_has_account_word.context: Password field status line: the password contains a word taken from the account's address, domain or display name.

password.problem_predictable.context: Password field status line: the strength estimate finds the password too easy to guess (repeats, runs such as abc or 1234, keyboard rows, one common word).

password.problem_too_long.context: Password field status line: the password is longer than allowed. {max} = the maximum length (256).

password.problem_too_short#one.context: Password field status line while typing: the password is too short, one character is missing. {count} = characters still missing, {min} = the minimum for this account.

password.problem_too_short#other.context: Password field status line while typing: the password is too short. {count} = characters still missing, {min} = the minimum for this account.

password.required.context: Password field status line, in red, after the person pressed Continue (or Change password) with the new password still empty. The rules sentence (password.rules) follows it on the same line.

password.rules.context: Password field status line while nothing is typed: the password rules, fixed by the Product Owner. {min} = minimum length for members (12), {adminMin} = minimum length for admins (16); both are numbers from constants.

password.rules_admin.context: Password rules under an empty password field of an ADMIN account (Setup's first account, an admin's own password). {min} = 16.

password.show.context: Button (icon only): eye icon inside every password field that shows the typed password; aria-label, no visible text. It keeps this name while the password is shown (its pressed state says so).

password.show_current.context: Button (icon only): eye icon inside the 'Current password' field of Change password; aria-label and tooltip.

password.show_new.context: Button (icon only): eye icon inside the field for a NEW password; aria-label and tooltip. Named after its field so it differs from the repeat field's button.

password.show_repeat.context: Button (icon only): eye icon inside the field where the new password is typed a second time; aria-label and tooltip.

password.suggest.context: Button under the password field on admin screens: fills in a generated passphrase (random words) and shows it. Shown with a wand icon.

password.suggest_another.context: Button under the password field on admin screens, after a passphrase was suggested: generates a different one. Shown with a wand icon.

password.suggest_hint.context: Hint shown under the Suggest button after a passphrase was filled in. {words} = how many random words the passphrase has (a number, 6).

prefs.density.context: Settings > Mail: title of the card that chooses how tall the message rows are (device preference).

prefs.density_comfortable.context: Settings > Mail > Density: the default choice (taller rows).

prefs.density_comfortable_hint.context: Settings > Mail > Density: what a comfortable row shows.

prefs.density_compact.context: Settings > Mail > Density: the choice with shorter rows.

prefs.density_compact_hint.context: Settings > Mail > Density: what the compact choice does.

prefs.device_only.context: Settings: line under the Motion and Keyboard headings; these choices are kept in this browser, not in the account

prefs.keyboard_title.context: Settings: heading of the keyboard shortcuts section

prefs.motion.context: Settings > Appearance: heading of the motion section (animations of this device)

prefs.motion_choice.context: Settings > Appearance > Motion: label of the two options (Match system, Reduce motion), read before each of them

prefs.motion_reduce.context: Settings > Appearance > Motion: option that turns animations down on this device

prefs.motion_reduce_hint.context: Settings > Appearance > Motion: one line under the Reduce motion option

prefs.motion_system.context: Settings > Appearance > Motion: option that follows the device's own reduce-motion setting

prefs.motion_system_hint.context: Settings > Appearance > Motion: one line under the Match system option

prefs.shortcuts.context: Settings > Keyboard: label of the on/off switch for shortcuts that are a single key (/, C, J, K)

prefs.shortcuts_hint.context: Settings > Keyboard: one or two lines under the single-key shortcuts switch

prefs.shortcuts_table.context: Settings > Keyboard: name of the table that lists the keyboard shortcuts (read by screen readers)

prefs.undo_action.context: Settings > Keyboard: what Ctrl+Z does (undo the archive, move or snooze of the toast on screen)

prefs.undo_send.context: Settings > Mail: title of the card that sets how long a sent message waits so it can be taken back.

prefs.undo_send_hint.context: Settings > Mail > Undo send: hint under the list. 'Send' and 'Undo' are the button names, 'Drafts' the folder name.

prefs.undo_send_label.context: Settings > Mail > Undo send: label of the list of times (Off, 5, 10, 20, 30 seconds).

prefs.undo_send_off.context: Settings > Mail > Undo send: the choice with no waiting time.

prefs.undo_send_seconds.context: Settings > Mail > Undo send: one choice of the list; {seconds} is 5, 10, 20 or 30.

push.blocked.context: Settings > Notifications error when the browser has notifications blocked for this site

push.dev_server.context: Settings > Notifications error in a development build, where the service worker is not registered

push.device_off_failed.context: Settings > Notifications error when turning notifications off on this device did not work

push.device_unknown.context: Settings > Notifications error after Send test: the push service dropped this device

push.no_device.context: Settings > Notifications error after Send test: no device is registered

push.not_allowed.context: Settings > Notifications error when the browser permission prompt was dismissed without an answer

push.service_rejected.context: Settings > Notifications error after Send test: the push service refused the notification

push.service_unreachable.context: Settings > Notifications error when the browser cannot reach its push service (e.g. Google, Apple, Mozilla)

push.test_failed.context: Settings > Notifications fallback error for Send test

push.turn_off_failed.context: Settings > Notifications fallback error for turning notifications off

push.turn_on_failed.context: Settings > Notifications fallback error for turning notifications on

reader.actions_label.context: Reader: accessible name of the toolbar of actions on the open message (Archive, Move to Trash, Snooze...). Not shown.

reader.add_label.context: Reader toolbar: aria-label and tooltip of the icon button that opens the label menu. Icon-only: no visible text.

reader.arrived_by_email.context: Reader: heading of the explanation (popover; bottom sheet on a phone) that the Unverified sender chip opens, on a received message that arrived over email from outside while its From address is one of THIS deployment's own domains (the organisation's): anyone on the internet can write such an address. Plain words for a non-expert; not an alarm; it does not say the message is fake.

reader.attachments_summary#one.context: Reader attachments heading, one file: {count} is 1, {size} is the total size such as "12 KB".

reader.attachments_summary#other.context: Reader attachments heading, several files: {count} files, {size} is the total size such as "1.2 MB".

reader.back_to_list.context: Reader toolbar, phone only: aria-label and tooltip of the icon button that goes back to the message list. Icon-only: no visible text.

reader.bar_delete.context: Reader on a phone, bottom bar (Trash and Spam): the words under the icon of Delete forever, saying it is permanent (J4-33); up to two short lines (its full name action.delete_forever is the accessible name; these words must be part of it).

reader.bar_inbox.context: Reader on a phone, bottom bar (Trash and Spam): the words under the icon of Move to Inbox, keeping the verb so it does not read as 'go to Inbox' (J4-33); up to two short lines; must be part of action.move_to_inbox.

reader.bar_more.context: Reader on a phone, bottom bar: short word under the More button (must be part of reader.more_actions).

reader.bar_trash.context: Reader on a phone, bottom bar: short word under the icon of Move to Trash (must be part of action.move_to_trash).

reader.bar_unread.context: Reader on a phone, bottom bar (Sent, Drafts): short word under the icon of Mark as unread (must be part of action.mark_unread).

reader.create_label.context: Label menu: aria-label and tooltip of the round + button that creates the typed label. Icon-only.

reader.download_all.context: Text button on the attachments line of the reader (2 or more files): saves every attachment, one after the other

reader.download_file.context: Reader attachments: accessible name and tooltip of one attachment card, which is its download (a long name wraps in the tooltip); {type} is the type shown on the card's tile (PDF, XLSX), {name} the file name, {size} its size as shown on the card. Keep {type}, {name}, {size} first, the card's visible text in its order, then the action: the name must start with the visible text (WCAG 2.5.3, voice control).

reader.hide_quoted.context: Reader: button under a received reply (plain text) and the control inside an HTML mail that folds the quoted original message away again; the pair of reader.show_quoted

reader.label_applied.context: Screen-reader announcement after a label was put on the open message from the Labels picker; {label} is the label's name

reader.label_exists.context: Label menu: red hint when a label with that name already exists (case-insensitive).

reader.label_invalid.context: Label menu: red hint under the new-label field when the name has a character that is not allowed (letters, numbers, space, - and _ are allowed).

reader.label_limit.context: Label menu: red hint when the message already has the most labels it may have. {max} is a fixed number (20).

reader.label_name_limit.context: Label menu: grey hint under the new-label field once the name has reached the longest allowed length. {max} is a fixed number (30).

reader.label_removed.context: Screen-reader announcement after a label was taken off the open message (Labels picker or the x of its chip); {label} is the label's name

reader.labels.context: Reader toolbar button (and the title of the picker it opens) that puts labels on the open message and takes them off: each label is a checkbox

reader.load_failed.context: Reader: heading shown in place of a message that could not be loaded; under it list.load_failed_hint and a Try again button.

reader.loading_message.context: Reader pane while the open message loads (spinner and text).

reader.mark_unread.context: Reader toolbar on a desktop: the words beside the envelope icon of Mark as unread when the pane has room (shorter than action.mark_unread, which stays its full name in menus)

reader.more_actions.context: Reader on a phone: aria-label and tooltip of the last button of the bottom bar; it opens a menu with Move to Spam, Mark as unread and Add label.

reader.nav_label.context: Reader on a phone: accessible name of the top row with Back, Newer message and Older message. Not shown.

reader.new_label.context: Label menu: placeholder and aria-label of the field where a new label name is typed (about 170 px wide, 16 px font).

reader.newer_message.context: Reader toolbar (desktop): aria-label and tooltip of the icon button that opens the next newer message. Icon-only: no visible text.

reader.no_subject.context: Reader heading when the message has no subject.

reader.none_selected.context: Reader pane title when no message is open (under the Edgar picture).

reader.none_selected_empty_hint.context: Reader pane line under 'No message selected' when the list beside it is empty (nothing to choose yet): where an opened message appears.

reader.none_selected_hint.context: Reader pane hint under the empty-state title.

reader.older_message.context: Reader toolbar (desktop): aria-label and tooltip of the icon button that opens the next older message. Icon-only: no visible text.

reader.remove_label.context: Screen-reader name and tooltip of the x button on a label chip in the reader's header; {label} is the label's name

reader.show_quoted.context: Reader: button under a received reply (plain text), and the control drawn inside an HTML mail, that shows the quoted original message folded away at the end of the reply (same words as compose.show_quoted)

reader.spam_notice.context: Quiet one-line notice under the header of a message opened in the Spam folder, beside a Move to Inbox button

reader.to_cc_line.context: Reader sender block, grey line when the message also has copy recipients: {to} and {cc} are addresses or lists of addresses.

reader.to_line.context: Reader sender block, grey line under the sender name: who the message was sent to. {to} is an address or a list of addresses. Lowercase on purpose (it reads like "to me").

reader.to_me.context: Reader sender block, grey line under the sender name when the signed-in person's own address is the only recipient (the address itself shows when the line is opened). Lowercase, like reader.to_line.

reader.unverified_note.context: Reader: the explanation of the Unverified sender chip, under its heading reader.arrived_by_email, above a Move to Spam button: why (an address of the organisation, but the message came from outside and nothing confirmed the sender) and what to be careful with. Calm, factual; it does not claim the message is fake.

reader.unverified_sender.context: Reader header: words of a quiet neutral chip on a message that arrived over email from outside while its From address is on one of THIS deployment's own domains; pressing it explains (reader.arrived_by_email + reader.unverified_note). Not an alarm; it does not say the message is fake.

reader.view_html.context: Reader: segmented switch above the body (shown only when the message has both forms): formatted (HTML) version. Technical word, may stay "HTML".

reader.view_label.context: Not shown: the name screen readers give the segmented switch between the HTML and the plain-text view of an open message.

reader.view_plain.context: Reader: segmented switch above the body: plain-text version of the message.

recovery.claim.context: The one security sentence on every recovery-key screen and inside the downloaded file. Exact claim of the design (15.1): nobody, admins included, can restore mail without the password or the recovery key.

recovery.confirm_button.context: Button: the person confirms they saved the recovery key; this sends the request that stores the keys.

recovery.confirm_lead.context: Asks the person to type back three groups of the key to show they saved it. {first}, {second} and {third} are group numbers (1 to 9, never neighbours).

recovery.confirm_mismatch.context: The typed groups were wrong; the next attempt asks for different groups.

recovery.copy_failed.context: Shown when the browser refused to copy the recovery key to the clipboard.

recovery.download.context: Button: saves the recovery key as a text file (secondary button next to Copy).

recovery.download_warning.context: Warning under the Copy and Download buttons: a downloaded file stays on the device; on iPhone and iPad the file opens in a viewer, so Copy is the way there.

recovery.file_title.context: First line of the downloaded recovery key text file. {address} is the person's email address. The product name stays as it is.

recovery.group_label.context: Small label above each of the nine groups of six characters of the recovery key, and above each box of the typed check. {number} is 1 to 9.

recovery.group_required.context: Recovery key check: red line under one of the three boxes where the person types back a group of the key, after the button was pressed with that box empty. {number} is the number of that group (1 to 9).

recovery.old_stops.context: Shown only when the new key replaces an earlier one: the old recovery key stops working ON THIS SERVER at once when the person finishes. The scope matters (PB-11): the mail key does not change, so an old copy of the stored data plus the old recovery key would still open old mail; do not translate it as "stops working" without "on this server".

recovery.problem_characters.context: Typed recovery key containing a character that is not part of the key alphabet.

recovery.problem_checksum.context: Typed recovery key whose two check characters do not match: a typing mistake, found before anything is sent.

recovery.problem_length.context: Typed recovery key with the wrong number of characters (54 in nine groups of six, hyphens and spaces ignored).

recovery.shown_once.context: Under the claim: the key is displayed one time only.

recovery.title_first.context: Heading of the screen that shows the recovery key for the first time (first sign-in, first-run setup).

recovery.title_new.context: Heading of the screen that shows a NEW recovery key (after 'Create a new recovery key' and after a forgotten-password recovery).

security.admin_claim_no_access.context: First sentence of the admin claim, shown where an admin role is chosen or confirmed and on the first-run Setup screen. Final wording from the Product Owner (addendum 4.12): word for word in every language. The old absolute wording ('Nobody ... admins included') is withdrawn.

security.admin_claim_operator.context: Last sentence of the admin claim, shown after security.admin_claim_setup_key. Keep it word for word in every language.

security.admin_claim_powers.context: Third sentence of the admin claim (after security.admin_claim_temp_password). CHANGED in batch 2b: it now also lists re-creating an address, moving aliases, and says the person is told when their two-factor sign-in is reset (the landing page says the same: 'the person is notified when their two-factor sign-in is reset'). Use the landing page's words for the same things. Word for word in every language.

security.admin_claim_setup_key.context: Fourth sentence of the admin claim, NEW in batch 2b. 'Setup key' is the deployment secret the person who deployed Edging Mail sets (APP_PASSWORD); it is the same term as in the Setup and break-glass screens (breakglass.setup_key). 'Console access' = being able to sign in to the admin console again. The restored admin gets a new key, so mail that arrived under the old key stays locked.

security.admin_claim_temp_password.context: Second sentence of the admin claim, always shown right after security.admin_claim_no_access. Final wording from the Product Owner (addendum 4.12): word for word in every language. 'Server key' is the key the server holds for mail that arrives before the person has signed in.

security.admin_delete_lost_keys.context: Delete account dialog: wording from the Product Owner, keep it word for word in every language.

security.badge_off.context: Settings > Security, card 'Two-factor sign-in': state badge next to the title when it is off (amber, with an alert icon).

security.badge_on.context: Settings > Security, card 'Two-factor sign-in': state badge next to the title when it is on (green, with a tick icon).

security.badge_saved.context: Settings > Security, row 'Recovery key': badge saying the account has a recovery key (it was saved when the account was set up).

security.cannot_turn_off_admin.context: Security card row 'Two-factor sign-in': shown instead of a Turn off button when the signed-in person is an admin.

security.cannot_turn_off_required.context: Security card row 'Two-factor sign-in': shown instead of a Turn off button when the organisation requires two-factor sign-in of everyone.

security.change_password.context: Button: Security card row 'Password' (opens the change-password form) and the submit button of that form.

security.codes_action.context: Button on the Security card 'Recovery codes' (only with two-factor sign-in on): starts getting a new set; the old set stops working.

security.codes_hint.context: Settings > Security, card 'Recovery codes' (only with two-factor sign-in on): the line under the title.

security.codes_lead.context: Paragraph above the password and code fields of the 'Get new recovery codes' form: the old recovery codes stop working.

security.codes_new_title.context: Settings > Security, the view that shows a fresh set of recovery codes after the form: its only heading (the replaced-codes note sits under it).

security.codes_replace_note.context: Shown above the new recovery codes list (after the form): the new codes replace the old ones.

security.current_password.context: Label of the first field of the change-password form: the password used now (the next two fields are the new one, gate.new_password and gate.repeat_password).

security.description.context: Settings > Security: one line under the page title.

security.devices_action.context: Button: Security card 'Other devices' (opens the form) and the submit button of that form. Signs out every other browser and phone of the account; this device stays signed in.

security.devices_done.context: Success message in Settings > Security after the other devices were signed out, with a Back button under it. This device stays signed in. Plain sentence, no question mark.

security.devices_hint.context: Settings > Security, card 'Other devices': the line under the title.

security.devices_lead.context: Lead line of the 'Sign out other devices' form, above the password field.

security.devices_title.context: Settings > Security: title of the card that signs out the other devices, and the heading of its form.

security.key_new_action.context: Button on the Security card 'Recovery key' (its name is read with the card title): starts creating a new key that replaces the old one.

security.key_new_done.context: Success message after the new recovery key was stored, with a Back button under it.

security.key_new_lead.context: Paragraph above the password field that starts making a new recovery key: it replaces the old one, the password and the mail stay as they are.

security.key_since.context: Settings > Security, row 'Recovery key': when the current recovery key was made (first sign-in, or the last replacement). {date} = date and time.

security.key_test_action.context: Button on the Security card 'Recovery key' (its name is read with the card title): opens the check of the saved key.

security.key_test_button.context: Button: submits the typed recovery key to the test (no request is sent; the check runs in the browser).

security.key_test_hint.context: Hint under the recovery key test field: the shape of a recovery key (54 characters in nine groups of six).

security.key_test_lead.context: Paragraph above the recovery key test field: what the test does, that it runs in this browser and sends nothing.

security.key_test_ok.context: Result of the recovery key test when the key is the current one.

security.key_test_required.context: Settings > Security > Test my recovery key: red line under the field after Test was pressed with it empty.

security.key_test_wrong.context: Result of the recovery key test when the key is well formed but is not the current one. Does not say how it differs.

security.key_tested_here.context: Settings > Security, row 'Recovery key': the last successful 'Test key' in this browser (the server is not told about tests). {date} = date and time.

security.new_codes.context: Button: Security card row 'Two-factor sign-in' (only when it is on): makes a new set of recovery codes; also the submit button of that form.

security.new_key.context: Button: Security card row 'Recovery key' (starts making a new recovery key that replaces the old one).

security.off_done.context: Success message after two-factor sign-in was turned off, with a Back button under it.

security.off_lead.context: Paragraph above the password and code fields of the form that turns two-factor sign-in off: says what is lost.

security.on_done.context: Success message after two-factor sign-in was turned on and the recovery codes were saved, with a Back button under it.

security.on_lead.context: Paragraph above the password field that starts turning on two-factor sign-in (the QR code screen follows).

security.other_devices_note.context: Note under the submit button of the new-recovery-codes and turn-off forms: this device stays signed in, every other device is signed out (the server ends the other sessions).

security.password_changed.context: Success message in Settings > Account > Security after the person changed their password, with a Back button under it. This device stays signed in; every other device was signed out. Plain sentence, no question mark.

security.password_hint.context: Settings > Security, card 'Password': the line under the title.

security.password_note.context: Plain note under the Change password button: what changing the password does and does not do.

security.password_required.context: Settings > Security: red line under the (current) password field after the person pressed the action's button with the field empty (change password, a new recovery key, turn two-factor sign-in on or off, new recovery codes).

security.recovery_hint.context: Settings > Account > Security: line under the 'Recovery key' row label: what the recovery key is for (forgot-password flow keeps the mail readable).

security.step_up_lead.context: Shown above the new recovery key when the server asks for a code from the authenticator app first: tells the person to type the six-digit code in the field below it.

send.changed_body.context: Body of that confirmation. Honest and calm: a changed key is normal after a person sets up their keys again, but it can also mean the key was replaced. 'Fingerprint' is a short number (6 groups of 5 digits) that identifies a key; the person can read it to the other one by phone or in person. Do not claim the key is safe or unsafe.

send.changed_confirm.context: Button of the key-changed confirmation: send, and remember the new key for this person. Not a question.

send.changed_line.context: One line block per person in that dialog: the address, then the fingerprint of the key used before ({before}) and of the new key ({now}); the fingerprints are groups of digits. Keep the three lines (separated by line breaks).

send.changed_title.context: Title of the confirmation shown when the encryption key of a recipient is not the one this browser remembered from earlier sends (key pinning, S3).

send.external_body.context: Body of that confirmation. {addresses} is one address per line. It must say the answer is sent without the protection of the message it answers (that message was encrypted in the sender's browser) and that quoted text leaves in the clear. Do not use the badge term 'end-to-end encrypted' here (a catalogue test allows it only on the e2e.badge keys). 'Edging Mail' is the product name and is never translated.

send.external_title.context: Title of the confirmation before answering or forwarding an end-to-end encrypted message to an address outside this Edging Mail (N6).

send.no_keys_body.context: Body of that confirmation. {addresses} is one address per line (one or several people); 'they' covers both. It must keep both facts: the server can read the message, and only until the person signs in and sets up encryption. Do not soften it into 'may'.

send.no_keys_inline.context: Extra paragraph in the confirmation before sending to a person who has not set up encryption yet (send.no_keys_body), shown only when the message has images placed inside the text. Their copy travels as plain text and loses the position of those images; they still receive the files. Calm, factual.

send.no_keys_title.context: Title of the confirmation before sending a message to a person on this Edging Mail who has never signed in (CK-1). Said calmly, not alarming.

send.send_anyway.context: Button that confirms sending although the situation in the dialog is not ideal (a recipient without keys, or a reply that leaves end-to-end encryption). Not a question.

send.too_big_body.context: Body of that confirmation: the message cannot be encrypted in the browser for everyone, so it can go the usual way, where the server can read it. Keep 'the server can read it' explicit.

send.too_big_confirm.context: Button that sends the message the usual way (not end-to-end encrypted). Not a question.

send.too_big_title.context: Title of the confirmation shown when a message is over the size limits of the end-to-end route (too large, too many files, too many recipients for the files).

send.was_keyed_body.context: Body of that confirmation. {addresses} is one address per line. Keep both consequences: the server can read the message, or it leaves as normal email. A legitimate cause exists (an admin deleted the keys, the account was re-created).

send.was_keyed_title.context: Title of the confirmation before sending to an address this browser sent ENCRYPTED mail to before, when the server now says it has no encryption keys or is not on this server (EC-2).

users.filter_two_factor_label.context: People page: accessible name of the two-factor filter (a list next to the status filter).

users.filter_two_factor_off.context: People page, two-factor filter: only the people without two-factor sign-in. A count may follow.

users.filter_two_factor_on.context: People page, two-factor filter: only the people who have two-factor sign-in. A count may follow.

users.last_sign_in.context: People table of the admin console, phone layout (rows stacked, no column headers): when the person last signed in. {when} is a date and time already formatted for the language.

users.loading.context: Admin People tab while the list loads (spinner and text).

users.make_admin.context: Button in the account dialog (and its confirm button): gives the person the admin role.

users.make_admin_desc.context: Person dialog: one line next to the Make admin button, saying what it does.

users.make_member.context: Button in the account dialog (and its confirm button): gives an admin the member role.

users.make_member_desc.context: Person dialog: one line next to the Make member button, saying what it does.

users.manage.context: People table: the quiet word at the end of each row that says the row opens the person (a picture of the action; the name is the button).

users.never.context: People table, Last sign-in column: the person never signed in.

users.new_account.context: Button above the people list, and title of the dialog it opens.

users.no_match.context: Admin People tab when a search finds nobody. {query} is the text the admin searched for.

users.not_signed_in_yet.context: Two places, one state: the Last sign-in cell of the People table when the person has never signed in, and the badge in the account dialog while the person has never signed in with their own password and has no keys yet (the only state in which an admin can issue a new temporary password).

users.password_saved.context: Button that closes the temporary password dialog (the only way to close it).

users.people_count#one.context: People page: the count at the end of the table when it lists everyone. {count} is a number.

users.people_count#other.context: People page: the count at the end of the table when it lists everyone. {count} is a number.

users.profile_heading.context: Person dialog: heading of the display name section.

users.reissue_desc.context: Person dialog of someone who never signed in: one line next to the Issue a new temporary password button.

users.reissue_temp_password.context: Button in the account dialog, shown only while the person has not signed in yet: issues a new temporary password (the old one stops working at once). Also the label of the confirm button.

users.reissued_title.context: Title of the admin dialog that shows a new temporary password for an existing account that has not signed in yet (after "Issue a new temporary password"). Not the title for a new account (users.created_title).

users.reset_scheduled.context: Line under the buttons of the admin dialog after an admin asked to reset the two-factor sign-in of ANOTHER ADMIN: it is scheduled, not done. {due} is a date and time.

users.reset_two_factor.context: Button in the account dialog (and its confirm button): resets the person's two-factor sign-in.

users.reset_two_factor_desc.context: Person dialog: one line next to the Reset two-factor sign-in button, saying when to use it and what follows.

users.reset_two_factor_none.context: Person dialog: next to the Reset two-factor sign-in button, which is turned off because the person has no two-factor sign-in.

users.role.context: New account dialog: legend of the radio group that picks Member or Admin. Also the header of the Role column of the People table in the admin console.

users.save_name.context: Button next to the display name field of the account dialog.

users.search_label.context: aria-label of the search field of the People tab. Screen reader only.

users.search_placeholder.context: Placeholder of the search field of the People tab (a search icon is before it and its label is Search people): what to type, short.

users.self_note.context: Account dialog, own account: why the disable, delete and reset buttons are missing.

users.showing.context: Admin People tab under the list: how many accounts are loaded of how many exist. {shown} and {total} are numbers.

users.status_active.context: Badge in the account dialog: the account is active.

users.status_disabled.context: Badge on an account that is disabled (user list row and account dialog).

users.temp_expires.context: Person dialog, under the badges: an account still on its temporary password. {when} is a date and time.

users.temp_password_expired.context: Admin People table, Last sign-in cell of a person who never signed in and whose temporary password already stopped working. {when} is a short date, e.g. "Nov 10".

users.temp_password_expires.context: Admin People table, Last sign-in cell of a person who never signed in and still has the temporary password an admin made: when it stops working. {when} is a short date, e.g. "Nov 19".

users.this_is_you.context: Account dialog: shown next to the badges when the admin opens their own account.

users.two_factor_is_off.context: Admin console: the person has no two-factor sign-in (stacked rows on a phone, the person's dialog).

users.two_factor_is_on.context: Admin console: a person's two-factor state where no column header names it (stacked rows on a phone, the person's dialog).

users.two_factor_off.context: People table, Two-factor column: this person has no two-factor sign-in.

users.two_factor_on.context: People table, Two-factor column: this person has two-factor sign-in set up.
